samples.question: The picture shows one solid black BAR near the top and four grey rails below it, one above the other. The four rails all start at the same left position and end at the same right position, and each rail is marked at both of its ends by a short downward grey stub. Standing on each rail is a row of solid blocks, all of them in that rail's own colour: one rail carries red blocks, one green, one blue and one orange. An EMPTY STRETCH of a rail is a piece of that rail with no block standing on it; the piece of rail between the left end and the first block, and the piece between the last block and the right end, are empty stretches too, exactly like the pieces between neighbouring blocks. A rail ACCEPTS the bar when at least one single empty stretch of that rail is wider than the black bar, so that the bar could be set down there without overlapping a block; only one empty stretch at a time may be used, and empty stretches on the same rail are never added together. In every picture exactly one of the four rails accepts the bar, and the bar is never the same width as any empty stretch. Only the widest single empty stretch of a rail matters. The rail with the most empty rail in total, the rail with the most blocks, the rail with the fewest blocks, the rail carrying the widest single block and the rail with the least block material are each the answer no more often than chance allows, and so is the topmost rail; the horizontal position of the black bar carries no information and only its width counts. Which rail accepts the bar? Answer red, green, blue or orange.
